title: The Borrowed Lantern
premise: In the final winter of the Vessarine Republic, Ulyana Eastwick carries sealed dispatches for a government that no longer exists, moving through occupied towns where loyalty is currency and truth is contraband. When an unknown woman leaves a child at her door with orders to forget the face, Ulyana discovers the girl's satchel holds proof of the massacre at Kelvane Bridge—evidence that could indict the occupying general or destroy what remains of the resistance. Pursued through three checkpoints by an old friend turned collaborator, Ulyana must choose between delivering her own dispatches and smuggling the child and the evidence to safety. In the end she burns her diplomatic credentials, delivers the evidence to a foreign press instead of a dead government, and takes the child north—not as a courier of history, but finally as a participant in it.
about_author: Dominic Crane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing displaced-persons records from twentieth-century border wars. The Borrowed Lantern is their second novel, written in rented rooms along old courier routes.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sealed Things
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She crosses into occupied Vessar with diplomatic papers and a practiced indifference, believing neutrality will protect her. Establishes her creed: history happens to other people. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath professional calm as she notices the roads emptier than her briefing promised.

chapters.title: A Knock Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A woman leaves a mute child, Mira, at her boarding-house door with a note: forget the face. Inside the girl's coat lining, Ulyana finds documents describing the Kelvane Bridge massacre. Emotional beat: terror disguised as irritation; her invisibility has been weaponized by a stranger's trust.

chapters.title: The Innkeeper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, with a flashback from the dying mother. Ulyana learns the woman was a resistance archivist who chose her precisely because Ulyana 'belongs to no one.' First checkpoint looms. Emotional beat: reluctant responsibility hardening into resolve as she reads the ledger of the dead.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: The Paper Face
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She passes the first checkpoint by performing the bureaucrat, Mira coached to be her silent niece—but a guard recognizes the massacre's location on a misdirected form. Emotional beat: the thrill of deception curdling when she realizes someone is now looking for them specifically.

chapters.title: An Old Friend's Uniform
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Ulyana and Tomas Brandt, her childhood friend now serving the occupation as an interrogator. He identifies her from a checkpoint sketch but delays the report, torn between duty and memory. Emotional beat: the ache of loyalty pulling two directions; both know one of them will betray the other.

chapters.title: The Lantern Keeper
chapters.summary: Mira's POV, first time. Hiding in a lighthouse keeper's cellar, the girl reveals she can speak—and that her mother made her memorize names, not just carry papers. Emotional beat: found family kindling; Ulyana stops being a courier and becomes a guardian, whether she consents or not.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A flooded crossing forces them onto a smuggler's barge; the captain demands the evidence as payment, and Ulyana bargains with half-truths while Tomas's agents close in. Emotional beat: desperation sharpening into cunning; she sacrifices her own dispatches to keep the massacre file intact.

chapters.title: The General's Invitation
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Summoned by General Aldous Reiner himself, Tomas realizes his superiors already know about the evidence and intend to bury it with everyone carrying it. He must decide whether warning Ulyana is treason or the last honest act available to him. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; justice and law fully divorced.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: The Burning Credentials
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, climax. At the final gate, Tomas lets them through and is arrested for it; Ulyana burns her diplomatic papers in the guardhouse stove to become untraceable, then doubles back to break him out. Emotional beat: fury and grief fused into action—she chooses people over mission, openly, irreversibly.

chapters.title: Northward, With Names
chapters.summary: Shared POV, resolution. They reach neutral territory; a foreign correspondent publishes the Kelvane file, and the republic's death becomes testimony instead of rumor. Ulyana formally takes guardianship of Mira; Tomas, exiled, lights the lantern in their new window each night. Emotional beat: sorrow transmuted into belonging—history no longer happens elsewhere.
